sentences.text: The tooth crown features a well-developed, high, pointed main cusp that inclines lingually in both juvenile and adult teeth. The lingual margin of the tooth crown overhangs the root, particularly near the apex. In occlusal view, the crown lacks distinct transversal crests. The crown features ornamentation including a longitudinal medio-labial ridge that sometimes bifurcates at the base to delimit the apron. Conspicuous short vertical ridges are present at the base of the labial crown.

The genus is known from a holotype antero-lateral tooth and several paratype teeth, including four from a single juvenile and one isolated tooth. Only one species, Iberotrygon plagiolophus, is known, and it was named and described in 2009.
The lingual face is steep and features a well-developed vertical uvula above a well-marked central depression.
Teeth of Iberotrygon show ontogenetic variation, differing between juvenile and adult stages.

The genus Iberotrygon was established by Kriwet, Nunn, and Klug in 2009. The species Iberotrygon plagiolophus was named by Kriwet, Nunn, and Klug in 2009. Iberotrygon belongs to the parent group Sclerorhynchiformes.
Iberotrygon lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
Iberotrygon teeth resemble those of Ptychotrygon, Texatrygon, and Archingeayia but can be easily distinguished by a specific combination of characters.
